title: Caching
summary: Where caches sit, what they cost, and how they fail: hit-rate math and sizing, cache-aside and its siblings, eviction, invalidation races, stampedes, negative caching, hot keys, and consistency with the source of truth.

units.title: Correctness: invalidation, stampedes, hot keys and consistency

labs.title: LRU cache with O(1) ops, TTL and cost weighting
Cache-aside with stampede protection (singleflight), negative caching and safe invalidation
LFU / TinyLFU-style admission with a count-min sketch

outcomes.text: Compute effective latency and backend load from a hit ratio, and explain why moving from a 95% to a 99% hit ratio is a 5x cut in backend load and a very different tail.

Place caches along a request path (browser, CDN, gateway, in-process, remote, database buffer pool) and choose between cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back, write-around and refresh-ahead, stating the failure semantics of each.
Choose an eviction policy (LRU, LFU, CLOCK, TinyLFU admission, TTL) for a workload and explain when scans, skew or one-hit wonders flip the answer.
Size a cache from working set, key skew and per-entry overhead, and decide whether the extra memory is worth the hit ratio it buys.
Implement an O(1) LRU with per-entry TTL on an injected clock, cost weighting, an eviction callback and concurrent safety (labs/a3/lru).
Reproduce the cache-aside stale-set race step by step, and design invalidation (delete after write, versioned keys, leases, short TTLs, event-driven invalidation) that bounds staleness.

Prevent stampedes with singleflight, TTL jitter, stale-while-revalidate, probabilistic early refresh and cache warming, and show why a cold cache must never be the only thing keeping the database alive.
Defend a cache against nonexistent keys (negative caching, Bloom filter) and hot keys (local L1, key replication), and know where the full hot-key treatment lives (A4).
Decide the acceptable staleness for each class of banking data, keep tenants' entries apart, and refuse to cache authorisation decisions blindly.
Implement a cache-aside loader with your own singleflight, negative and error caching, jitter, safe invalidation and stale-while-revalidate (labs/a3/cacheaside).
Operate a cache: pick the metrics that matter (hit ratio, eviction rate, p99, key cardinality), and plan for failover, memory pressure and loss of the whole cache.
Implement frequency-aware admission with a count-min sketch and show scan resistance against plain LRU (labs/a3/lfu).
